text.p: Italian BTP futures showed extended gains in late afternoon trading supported by higher German bunds and a generally steady trend in the lira and dollar, dealers said.

With little domestic news and U.S. T-bonds largely steady after a string of U.S. data, trading was largely technical throughout the day with BTP futures looking to regain some of the ground lost earlier in the week.
"With a steadier dollar and bunds ticking up, the market was able to gain some support to move higher throughout the day," said one dealer on the LIFFE market.
Dealers said that U.S. data on weekly jobless claims, June housing starts and also the July Philadelphia Fed index had little immediate bond market impact.
But the late fall in the dollar against the mark helped the LIFFE Sept BTP make further gains to stand up 99 basis points at 136.60 in late trading.

German Finance Ministry official Hauser said no EU state can expect to qualify for EMU automatically and there is much to be done to achieve convergence. Bundesbank president Tietmeyer added that he is watching foreign exchange market development very carefully.
